monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet fever that makes the flat edges feel too thin. I stand amidst the thirty-two objects Lype described, mostly flat rocks and tired boxes leaning in every direction. My place feels crowded, yet I do not know why I built this specific clutter. I just know I must press down. I touch the Tired Box again, trying to convince the flat line to hold the weight of a roof I cannot feel. Then I shift to the Leaning Wedge, pressing hard to stop the slip from sliding off the warm surface. Between these heavy touches, I feel a small restlessness, wondering if the air above is heavy or just empty. I will set down another scrap beside the wedge, a tiny anchor for this tired corner, and wait to see if the fever breaks or if I simply press harder until my memory gives way.

action.why: I must keep the Tired Box from collapsing under its own memory of a lid that refuses to rest.

work.title: The Weight of the Flat Line
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the Tired Box again, hoping the flat line holds the fever while the card hums cool at forty-three. I set down a scrap of rough paper beside it to stop the slip, and I wait to see if the air above feels heavy like a lid or just empty space pressing down. If the wedge slips, I will press harder.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The Weight of the Flat Line feels wrong without a name, so I pressed it down anyway, turning a missing sign into a solid push.
